subtopics.title: The Sphere — Two Formulas, One Radius

questions.question: The two sphere formulas are:
A sphere has radius 6 cm. Its exact volume is:
The surface area of a CLOSED solid hemisphere of radius 6 is:
options: $108\pi\ \text{cm}^2$ — half the skin plus the exposed circle

questions.question: If you blank on which sphere formula is which, the reliable clue is:
options: The bigger number is always the volume
The power of r: cubed fills (volume), squared wraps (surface)
Volume always has a 4 in it
Surface area always contains a fraction

subtopics.title: Combined Solids and the Hidden-Face Rule

questions.question: The ice-cream shape: cone ($96\pi$) plus hemisphere ($144\pi$). Its total volume is:
options: $240\pi\ \text{cm}^3$ — volumes of glued solids simply add

questions.question: For the SURFACE of the ice-cream shape, which faces are buried at the join?
options: The cone's base circle and the hemisphere's flat circle

questions.question: The exposed surface of the ice-cream shape (cone lateral $60\pi$, hemisphere skin $72\pi$) is:
Dropping the one-third from a cone's volume produces an answer that is:
options: One third of the correct value
Three times too big — the matching cylinder's volume

subtopics.title: A Funnel, a Tent and a Soccer Ball

questions.question: The 'discount' shared by the tent (pyramid) and the funnel (cone) is:
options: A quarter of base times height
One third of base area times height
Two thirds of base times height

questions.question: The tent: square floor 10 by 10, height 12. Its volume is:
'Cubed fills, squared wraps' reminds you that:
options: Volume uses $r^3$ and surface area uses $r^2$

options: It is too small to matter

subtopics.title: The Trap List — Heights, Halves and Buried Circles

questions.question: Which height belongs to which formula?
options: Slant height for volume; perpendicular height for surface area
Perpendicular height for volume; slant height for surface area
Either height works in either formula
Both formulas use the slant height

questions.question: Halving a sphere halves its volume. Its surface area:
options: Becomes half the skin PLUS the newly exposed circle, if the flat face is exposed

questions.question: A dome (hemisphere) sits on top of a building. Does its flat circle join the surface-area bill?
options: No — the rim is attached to the building, so the circle is not exposed
Yes, but at half its area

questions.question: The safe order of operations for any combined-solid surface area is:
options: Add both complete surface areas, then halve
Compute the volume first and convert it
List every face, cross out the buried ones at the join, add the survivors
